UULTIS /MATERIALS / 3 MIN READ

Materials in conversation.

Build a palette through grain, texture and the light around a piece.

Uultis digital experience · Editorial guide

IN THIS ARTICLEChoose a starting point.Let each surface play a role.Look at edges and transitions.Use digital finishes to explore a direction.

Choose a starting point.

Look for one material already present in your room: the floor, a wall surface or a favorite object. Use that as a reference when comparing furniture finishes. You can look for continuity or introduce a deliberate change in tone and texture.

Let each surface play a role.

Wood grain, woven upholstery, glass and metal offer different visual cues. In the collection, Li pairs a wood-veneer top with a stainless-steel base. Plot brings together a solid-wood structure, natural cotton-based weaving and clear glass. Compare the product photographs to see how these materials meet.

Look at edges and transitions.

Instead of looking only at the overall color, inspect the junction between a top and its base, the thickness of an edge and the way upholstery meets the frame. Those details often explain the character of a piece more clearly than a distant room photograph.

Use digital finishes to explore a direction.

The studio’s wood and textile controls are illustrative palettes, not an availability chart or a color guarantee. Screens, room light and natural variation affect what you see. Request the available finish options and material samples for the exact product before making a final selection.
